steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Defences allow a defendant to avoid criminal liability even if the prosecution has proved actus reus and mens rea

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Self-defence is available where the defendant used reasonable force to defend themselves, another person or property

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The force used must be proportionate to the threat — excessive force negates the defence of self-defence

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Insanity is governed by the M'Naghten rules — the defendant must have a defect of reason from a disease of the mind

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always identify whether the defence negates actus reus or mens rea — or is a general defence Self-defence is a complete defence — know the two-stage test (honest belief + reasonable force) The distinction between insanity and automatism turns on internal vs external causes — know this clearly Duress limitations are a favourite exam topic — know what crimes it cannot be used for Use case names to support your answers where possible — e.g. M'Naghten for insanity, Palmer for self-defence
